## Professional positioning {.section-title}

<div class="section-lead">
My professional objective is to build a portfolio that signals readiness for high-standard quantitative environments: markets, model risk, quantitative research, financial engineering, and technology teams where analytical rigor must be converted into production-quality tools.
</div>

<div class="card-grid">
  <div class="card span-4">
    <h3>Quantitative research</h3>
    <p>
      Research agenda centered on macro-financial shocks, deposit funding stability, exchange-rate stress, monetary transmission, systemic risk networks, and liquidity-risk measurement.
    </p>
  </div>

  <div class="card span-4">
    <h3>Quantitative development</h3>
    <p>
      Production-oriented implementation using Python, R, C++, Quarto, Git, automated testing, reproducible pipelines, model documentation, and deployment-ready analytical workflows.
    </p>
  </div>

  <div class="card span-4">
    <h3>Institutional impact</h3>
    <p>
      A decision-oriented approach: models are designed not only to estimate parameters, but to monitor risk, explain mechanisms, stress scenarios, and support senior-level decisions.
    </p>
  </div>
</div>

## Selected work {#selected-work .section-title}

<div class="section-lead">
The following projects are designed as flagship signals: each one combines econometric depth, computational discipline, financial interpretation, and reproducible delivery.
</div>

<div class="card-grid">
  <div class="card project-card span-6">
    <div class="project-meta">Flagship research system</div>
    <h3>Macro-Financial Risk Engine</h3>
    <p>
      A reproducible platform for monitoring macro-financial stress, funding fragility, FX pressure, and policy-shock transmission using high-frequency financial and macroeconomic data.
    </p>
    <ul>
      <li>GARCH-X volatility models with exogenous macro-financial regressors.</li>
      <li>Event-study modules for monetary-policy and liquidity shocks.</li>
      <li>Rolling betas, conditional volatility dashboards, and stress indicators.</li>
      <li>Quarto reports with automated tables, figures, and executive summaries.</li>
    </ul>
  </div>

  <div class="card project-card span-6">
    <div class="project-meta">Funding stability research</div>
    <h3>Deposit Funding Stability Lab</h3>
    <p>
      Empirical research program on deposit behavior by economic agent and currency denomination, treating daily deposit flows as informative signals of liquidity, currency preference, and risk perception.
    </p>
    <ul>
      <li>Agent-level heterogeneity: households, firms, financial sector, public sector, non-residents.</li>
      <li>Local-currency vs foreign-currency deposit dynamics.</li>
      <li>Core, stable, and structural deposit concepts for liquidity-risk and IRRBB analysis.</li>
      <li>Confidential-data safe design using anonymized, synthetic, or public examples.</li>
    </ul>
  </div>

  <div class="card project-card span-6">
    <div class="project-meta">Network econometrics</div>
    <h3>Systemic Risk Network Platform</h3>
    <p>
      A bank-borrower network framework for studying contagion, credit concentration, liquidity-shock propagation, and network-amplified macro-financial risk.
    </p>
    <ul>
      <li>Bipartite and projected network construction.</li>
      <li>Network-augmented local projections and event-study models.</li>
      <li>Contagion simulation and exposure concentration metrics.</li>
      <li>R/Python modules with reproducible documentation and tests.</li>
    </ul>
  </div>

  <div class="card project-card span-6">
    <div class="project-meta">Quant dev portfolio</div>
    <h3>High-Performance Quant Toolkit</h3>
    <p>
      A modular library of numerical and statistical tools for quantitative finance: simulation, backtesting, volatility estimation, model diagnostics, and risk analytics.
    </p>
    <ul>
      <li>C++/Rcpp acceleration for Monte Carlo simulation and matrix-intensive routines.</li>
      <li>Python pipelines for feature engineering, ML signals, SHAP explainability, and backtesting.</li>
      <li>Robust software practices: CI, unit tests, benchmarks, documentation, and versioning.</li>
      <li>Clear separation between research notebooks and production-ready modules.</li>
    </ul>
  </div>
</div>

    </p>

## Confidentiality and reproducibility {.section-title}

<div class="note-box">
All public work should use public, synthetic, or anonymized data. Internal banking, supervisory, client-level, credentialed, or institution-specific material should never be published. The portfolio is designed to demonstrate methodology, engineering discipline, and financial reasoning without exposing confidential information.
